Jen (Support): heads up — StellarDocs reported intermittent 503s starting 2024-08-02 09:12 UTC during a heavy login burst. Ticket SD-3821.
Marco (Oncall): @Jen looking. Any stack traces or pod IDs?
Jen (Support): pasted logs from customer-proxy:
```
2024-08-02T09:12:14Z infer-runner[pid=1234]: SIGSEGV at 0x7ff...
RuntimeError: cudaRuntimeError: out of memory
```
Jen (Support): pod: infer-runner-7d9f4, node: gpu-21
Steph (Engineer): grabbing kube logs now — seeing repeated OOM kills + live container restarts. `kubectl get pods` shows CrashLoopBackOff.
Steph (Engineer): `kubectl logs infer-runner-7d9f4 -n hosted | tail -n 200` ->
```
E tensorflow: out of memory allocating 2.3G
fatal: runtime: out of memory
Aborted (core dumped)
```
Marco (Oncall): @Rachel any recent model/quant swap or kernel changes in staging that could explain mem regress?
Rachel (ML Infra): We pushed a dynbatch tweak yesterday and landed a KV prefetch change that increases prefetch window under auth-heavy bursts. Could be memory pressure.
Tom (Infra): Node gpu-21 shows GPU mem at 98% and several containers restarted within 2m. I temporarily cordoned node and drained pods to mitigate.
Jen (Support): Customer impact: ~20% of requests returning 503, auth retries causing billing double-counts in some sessions. CS flagged potential billing break.
Ali (Customer Success): We put a temporary note to StellarDocs and offered credits; they want repro steps and ETA.
Steph (Engineer): Quick mitigation: rollback dynbatch tweak and disable KV prefetch on hosted route for StellarDocs. Will open canary rollout.
Marco (Oncall): Rollback in progress — `deploy rollback -s hosted -p runtime-config --to=2024-08-01` (ETA 6m)
Steph (Engineer): Also adding temporary route rule to split StellarDocs to fallback variant model-smaller for lower mem.
Rachel (ML Infra): For repro: run a synthetic auth-burst of 800 qps with long-context prompts and toolcalls; the sequence triggers prefetch thundering.
Rachel (ML Infra): repro script stub:
```
# heavy auth + long prompt load
for i in $(seq 1 800); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"<long 8k prompt>","stream":false}' &
done
wait
```
Tom (Infra): Post-rollback, node gpu-21 still had one OOM crash; I'm restarting runtime service on node and monitoring.
Steph (Engineer): Follow-ups: capture core dump, gdb backtrace, nvml logs, and heap profiles. Tagging `#SD-3821` in PR.
Marco (Oncall): If rollback fails, activate fallback routing to Dedicated pool for StellarDocs. ops-bot: open incident on-call playbook.
ops-bot: Incident created INC-2024-4875 and pager sent to eng-sre.
Jen (Support): Customer updated with ETA ~20m and steps. Thank you — will keep thread updated.
Marco (Oncall): last checks — p95 latency normalized after rollback; keeping throttles and node cordon for 30m.
Steph (Engineer): saving logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2024-4875/ for postmortem.
Ali (Customer Success): Customer accepted credits and will retest after 30m.
Jen (Support): closing initial escalation but keeping monitoring window open. :thumbsup:
